events.summary:
The combination of hot temperatures and humidity will produce
heat index values between 105 and 110 degrees for several hours
this afternoon into this evening. A few locations may briefly
experience heat index values above 111 degrees.

weight and light colored clothing, and take frequent breaks from
the heat. Young children and pets should never be left unattended
in vehicles.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Western Rogue Basin including the Illinois Valley; Siskiyou Mountains; Eastern Rogue Valley; Southern Oregon Cascades
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.

* AFFECTED AREA...In Oregon, Fire Weather zones 620, 621, 622,
and 623, including Medford, Grants Pass, Ashland, Cave
Junction, Eagle Point, Shady Cove, and the Siskiyous and
southern Oregon Cascades.

* WIND...Northwest 10 to 15 mph with gusts up to 25 mph in the
afternoons, becoming east to northeast overnight.

* HUMIDITY...Minimum humidity 8 to 15 percent, with poor
recoveries as low as 20 percent.

* ADDITIONAL INFORMATION...Critical fire weather conditions
will be more prevalent in low-lying areas in the afternoons
and evenings due to elevated breezes and minimum RHs.
Overnight and into early morning hours, area peaks and
ridgelines will have critical conditions due to easterly flow
and poor recoveries. Increasingly unstable conditions are
expected Wednesday, which could further increase fire
activity.

* DETAILED URL...View the hazard area in detail at
https://weather.gov/wrh/hazards?wfo=mfr

events.region: Beaverhead, MT; Deer Lodge, MT; Granite, MT; Lake, MT; Madison, MT; Mineral, MT; Missoula, MT; Powell, MT; Ravalli, MT; Sanders, MT; Silver Bow, MT
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
AQAMT

The Montana Department of Environmental Quality has issued an air
quality alert for Beaverhead, Deer Lodge, Granite, Lake, Madison,
Mineral, Missoula, Powell, Ravalli, Sanders, and Silver Bow counties
in effect until 9AM on 08/05/2026
An Air Quality Alert means that particulates have been trending
upwards and that an exceedance of the 24 hour National Ambient Air
Quality Standard (NAAQS) has occurred or may occur in the near
future.

Elevated particulate levels due to wildfire smoke

As of 6AM on 08/04/2026, particulate levels in Billings, Butte,
Columbia Falls, Cut Bank, Dillon, Frenchtown, Great Falls, Hamilton,
Helena, Libby, Missoula, Sleeping Giant and Thompson Falls are
Moderate.

When air quality is Moderate... State and local health officials
recommend that unusually sensitive people should consider reducing
prolonged or heavy exertion.

For more information visit the Montana Department of Environmental
Quality at http://todaysair.mtdeq.us

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Dare, NC
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southeastern Dare County in eastern North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Water over roadways. Overflowing poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 852 AM EDT, North Carolina Department of Transportation
reported deep standing water along portions of NC 12 from Oregon
Inlet to the Waves, Salvo, and Rodanthe areas. Water has been
reported to be up to the headlights of some vehicles. Between 4
and 7 inches of rain have fallen.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Rodanthe, Waves, Salvo and Hatteras Island Fishing Pier.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
